haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: 7 consecutive days under 0.1 percent mismatch and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move.
haiku-low.q4: Automatic rollback starts when new-engine charge failures exceed 2 percent in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only with gate counters reset. The new engine must again pass shadow and both gates, starting from zero.
haiku-low.q6: From day 35 onward, because skipped usage events have aged out of the 35-day log.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode before each charge without caching. An invoice mid-processing: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Gate values come from per-customer nightly results in the shadow store. A person checks the gate; config service enforcement is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q9: Detecting component: NOT STATED. It measures new-engine charge failure rate per 10-minute window and starts rollback, with no person gating it.
haiku-low.q10: Delayed, not dropped. Due charges are made at rollback step 4, after the old engine looks up each customer and period at the provider.
haiku-low.q11: Reconcile step: a period the new engine charged is not charged again. Old engine looks up provider before charging each due period.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays at that step with new charges frozen and on-call alerted. On-call checks the provider, then restarts the step by hand; no retry.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine writes its invoices to the shadow store (it never charges or writes the ledger).
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging, so it can take over at any time.
sonnet.q3: Gate: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1 percent and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move.
sonnet.q4: An automatic trigger: new-engine charge failure rate above 2 percent in any 10-minute window. It applies in both and new_only (new_only only on days 0 to 34), not in shadow.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only with gate counters reset. The path to shadow then starts again from zero (and then the gates must be met again for each forward move).
sonnet.q6: On day 35 or later in new_only. The skipped usage events have aged out of the 35-day log, so the old engine cannot recompute them.
sonnet.q7: Workers read billing_mode from the config service before each charge and do not cache it. What happens to an invoice being processed at the moment of a change is NOT STATED (open question about flag timing and double charging).
sonnet.q8: Gate values are computed from nightly comparison results stored per customer in the shadow store. Only the person checking the gate stops early promotion; whether the config service enforces gates is NOT STATED (open question).
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. The condition is new-engine charge failure rate above 2 percent over any 10-minute window (denominator is an open question); when met, an automatic rollback starts with no person gating it, running the same steps via the rollout controller.
sonnet.q10: Due charges wait (are delayed, not dropped) during rollback steps 1 to 3. They are made in step 4 when billing_mode is set to old_only and the old engine resumes charging, after looking up each customer and period at the provider.
sonnet.q11: Step 3 reconciliation: a period the new engine charged is not charged again; only periods with an invoice and no provider charge are marked due. Also the old engine looks up each due period at the provider before charging, and step 5 verifies no duplicate charges.
sonnet.q12: Stop at that step, new charges stay frozen, and on-call is alerted (billing_mode keeps its current value during steps 1 to 3). On-call looks up the provider for an existing charge for that customer and period, then restarts the step by hand. Never charge on a guess.
